components.title: Button
components.description: Spring press, ripple, icons and a stateful variant.
components.readme:
# Button

Native port of [beUI Button](https://beui.dev/components/motion/button). A spring-pressed `Button` plus `StatefulButton`, with the same variants, sizes and motion tokens as the web library.

```tsx
import { Button, StatefulButton } from "./src";

<Button onPress={save}>Save changes</Button>
<Button variant="secondary" startIcon={Plus}>Create project</Button>
<Button endIcon={ArrowRight}>Continue</Button>
<Button size="icon" variant="ghost" icon={Heart} accessibilityLabel="Add to favorites" />

<StatefulButton state={state} loadingText="Saving" successText="Saved" icon={ArrowRight}>
  Save changes
</StatefulButton>
```

## Button

- **Variants:** `primary`, `secondary`, `outline`, `ghost`.
- **Sizes:** `sm`, `md`, `lg` (32, 40 and 48 points tall) and `icon` (32-point square). Default `hitSlop` tops each up to a 48-point touch area. Native hit areas cannot extend past their parent, so leave room around compact buttons. Content can grow taller for larger text.
- **Press:** scales to `pressScale` (0.93 by default) on beUI's `SPRING_PRESS` spring, and springs back on release. With a mouse or trackpad (web, iPad), hovering lifts the button to 1.02.
- **Ripple:** `ripple` sends a soft wave out from the press point. It is off by default.
- **Reduced motion:** when the system asks for reduced motion, or `disableAnimation` is set, scale and ripple turn off and pressing dims the button instead.
- **Disabled:** dims to 50% opacity and reports the disabled state to accessibility services.

The label is the text child; interpolated text such as `<Button>Save {count} items</Button>` works. Icons go in `startIcon` and `endIcon`, which can be used together and follow the layout direction. `size="icon"` takes `icon` instead of a label and requires `accessibilityLabel` in TypeScript.

An icon can be a component that receives `{ size, color }`, such as a `lucide-react-native` icon or your own SVG component, or a prebuilt element. Pass a component defined outside render. An inline arrow function is a new component type on every render, so it remounts each time. Icons receive the button's icon size and foreground color, and are hidden from accessibility services because the button owns the spoken name.

`className` and `style` style the button itself. The button forwards Pressable props, handlers and its ref. Resolve conflicting utilities through `style` rather than class order.

## StatefulButton

`state` takes `idle`, `loading`, `success` or `error`. Text for each state comes from `children`, `loadingText`, `successText` and `errorText`.

- The label rolls letter by letter on `SPRING_SWAP`, and the button's width springs to fit the new text.
- A leading spinner, check or cross grows in beside the label. Replace them with `loadingIcon`, `successIcon` and `errorIcon`.
- The optional trailing `icon` shows only while idle.
- `loading` disables the button and reports busy.
- Each state change is announced to VoiceOver and TalkBack. The accessible name follows the current text unless you pass `accessibilityLabel`.
- Reduced motion swaps the cascade for a short crossfade, and the width changes without animating. The spinner keeps turning, because it shows that work is still in progress.
- Only Latin labels cascade. Splitting a label into letters breaks shaping in Arabic, Devanagari, Thai and other connected scripts, so those labels slide as a whole.

The web version also blurs letters as they move. Native has no cheap blur, so letters use opacity and position only.

## Copying

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `hooks/use-presence.ts`, `primitives/render-icon.tsx`, `primitives/cascade-text.tsx`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`. The host app needs React Native, Uniwind and Reanimated, set up as described in the root README.

## Validation

Before release, check on iOS and Android devices:

- VoiceOver and TalkBack announcements
- Large text
- RTL layouts
- Presses cancelled by scrolling
- Changing reduced motion while the app is open

components.title: Expandable Control
components.description: Buttons and chips that spring open to reveal more.
components.readme:
# Expandable Control

Native port of [beUI Expandable Control](https://beui.dev/components/motion/expandable-control). A round icon button and a chip that spring open when pressed, revealing a label or a trailing action, and fold back on the next press.

```tsx
import { ExpandableButton, ExpandableChip } from "./src";

<ExpandableButton icon={BellIcon} label="Notifications" />

<ExpandableChip
  label="React"
  actionLabel="Remove React"
  onAction={() => removeTag("react")}
/>
```

## ExpandableButton

A 44-point round button with an icon that grows into a pill showing its label.

- `icon`: a component given `{ size, color }`, or an element. `label`: the revealed text, also its accessible name.
- `expanded` / `defaultExpanded` / `onExpandedChange`: controlled or uncontrolled. Control it to keep one button in a group open at a time.
- `onPress` runs first; call `event.preventDefault()` in it to keep the button from toggling.
- `disabled`, `disableAnimation`, `className`, `labelClassName`, plus Pressable props.

## ExpandableChip

A 40-point chip whose label, when pressed, makes room for a trailing action.

- `label`, `actionLabel` (the action's accessible name, such as "Remove React"), `onAction`.
- `actionIcon`: replaces the default X.
- `collapseOnAction`: folds the chip after the action runs. Defaults to true.
- `expanded` / `defaultExpanded` / `onExpandedChange`, `disabled`, `disableAnimation`, `className`, `labelClassName`.

## Motion

One spring drives each control: a 0 to 1 progress (stiffness 320, damping 22, mass 0.8), quicker than the web version's continuity spring, like a native control under a finger, with a hint of give at the end. The width, the revealed content's fade and 8-point slide, and the surface's tint all read from it, so folding is opening played backward, overshoot included, and a tap mid-motion reverses from wherever it is.

- The button grows by its label's measured width. As a fold overshoots past closed, its outline dips a few points narrower while the icon stays centered and full size.
- The chip's action slot opens as its label's trailing padding gives room back, and its X turns in a quarter turn as it appears.
- Open controls take a soft tint and a firmer outline, so they read as on at a glance.
- Pressing sinks either to 96% on beUI's press spring.

The web version blurs content as it appears; React Native has no cheap blur, so it fades and slides instead. With reduced motion, or `disableAnimation`, controls change at once and the press doesn't scale.

For haptics, call your haptics library from `onExpandedChange`, as the showcase does with expo-haptics. To animate a chip out of a list when its action removes it, wrap it in an `Animated.View` with an `exiting` animation and a `layout` transition, and pass `collapseOnAction={false}`.

## Accessibility

The button and the chip's label report whether they're expanded. The chip's action is hidden from screen readers and can't be pressed while the chip is folded.

Copy this directory, `primitives/drawn-path.tsx`, `primitives/render-icon.tsx`, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`.

components.title: Card
components.description: Composable surfaces, selectable with press feedback.
components.readme:
# Card

Native port of [beUI Card](https://beui.dev/components/motion/card). A surface built from parts, with an optional pressable, selectable state.

```tsx
import {
  Card,
  CardAction,
  CardContent,
  CardDescription,
  CardFooter,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
} from "./src";

<Card>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle heading>Review order</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>Check the details before you confirm.</CardDescription>
    <CardAction>
      <Button variant="ghost" size="sm">Edit</Button>
    </CardAction>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>…</CardContent>
  <CardFooter className="justify-end">
    <Button size="sm">Confirm order</Button>
  </CardFooter>
</Card>
```

## Parts

- **Card:** the surface. `variant` is `outlined` (border on the page background, the default) or `muted` (a filled surface). `size` is `default` (24-point padding and gaps) or `compact` (16 points).
- **CardHeader:** stacks a title and description, and pins any `CardAction` child to the top trailing corner.
- **CardTitle** and **CardDescription:** the heading and supporting text. `heading` reports the title as a heading for screen readers.
- **CardContent** and **CardFooter:** the body, and a row for actions.

The card owns the vertical padding and the gap between parts. Each part pads itself horizontally, so any part can be left out, and media can run edge to edge: give the card `className="overflow-hidden pt-0"` and put an image first.

## Pressable and selectable cards

Give `Card` an `onPress` and the whole card becomes one touch target. Pressing sinks it to 98.5% on beUI's press spring. With reduced motion, or `disableAnimation`, pressing dims it instead.

`selected` fades in a 2-point primary outline over 200 ms and reports the selected state. For a card that acts as a checkbox or radio, let the card own the state and describe it:

```tsx
<Card
  selected={checked}
  onPress={() => setChecked(!checked)}
  accessibilityRole="checkbox"
  accessibilityState={{ checked }}
  accessibilityLabel="Signed contract"
>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Signed contract</CardTitle>
    <CardAction style={{ pointerEvents: "none" }} importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants">
      <Checkbox checked={checked} />
    </CardAction>
  </CardHeader>
</Card>
```

The control inside then only shows the state, so it shouldn't respond to touches or be read separately. That replaces the web version's stretched-target class: on native, the whole card is the touch target.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`.

components.readme:
# Input

Native port of [beUI Input](https://beui.dev/components/motion/input). A text field with a label, leading and trailing icons, an error shake, and a check that draws itself on success.

```tsx
import { Input } from "./src";

<Input
  label="Email"
  leftIcon={Mail}
  value={email}
  onChangeText={setEmail}
  error={valid ? undefined : "Enter a valid email address."}
  reserveErrorLine
/>
<Input label="Search" leftIcon={Search} success={found} />
<Input label="Password" secureTextEntry rightIcon={<ToggleButton />} />
```

- **Field:** a 44-point, fully rounded field. Its border fades between idle, focused and error colours over 200 ms. Focus and error also show a 2-point ring, like the web's `ring-2`.
- **Error:** a truthy `error` shakes the field (6, 4 and 2 points over 450 ms) and turns it red. A string `error` also shows a message that fades and drops in, and is announced to screen readers. `reserveErrorLine` keeps one line of space so content below doesn't jump.
- **Success:** `success` draws a check at the trailing edge in place of `rightIcon`.
- **Icons:** `leftIcon` and `rightIcon` take a component given `{ size, color }` (such as a lucide icon) or a prebuilt element. A trailing control, such as a show-password button, sits in a 44-point square so it stays easy to tap.
- **State:** pass `value` with `onChangeText` to control it, or `defaultValue` to let it manage itself. Every other `TextInput` prop passes through, and `ref` reaches the `TextInput`.
- **Accessibility:** the label is the field's spoken name, and pressing the label focuses the field. The error message is read as the hint and reported as invalid.
- **Reduced motion:** when the system asks for it, or `disableAnimation` is set, colours change instantly, nothing shakes, and the check appears fully drawn.

`classNames` styles the root, label, field, input and error message individually.

## Keyboard

- **Theme:** the keyboard follows the app's light or dark theme on iOS. Pass `keyboardAppearance` to override it.
- **Text:** text and placeholder sit centred in the 44-point field on every platform. The field sets a font size without a line height, because a line height on a `TextInput` pushes the text down on iOS.
- **Moving between fields:** `ref` reaches the `TextInput`, so set `returnKeyType="next"`, `submitBehavior="submit"` and `onSubmitEditing={() => nextRef.current?.focus()}`.
- **Autofill:** pass `autoComplete` and `textContentType` so iOS and Android can fill passwords, emails and one-time codes.
- **Staying above the keyboard:** that's the screen's job, not the field's. Since Android became edge-to-edge, the window no longer resizes when the keyboard opens, so use [react-native-keyboard-controller](https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v57.0.0/sdk/keyboard-controller/): wrap the app in `KeyboardProvider`, put forms in a `KeyboardAwareScrollView` with a `bottomOffset`, and add `KeyboardToolbar` for previous, next and done controls. The example app does exactly this.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-presence.ts`, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `hooks/use-shake.ts`, `primitives/drawn-path.tsx`, `primitives/render-icon.tsx`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`.

components.readme:
# OTP Input

Native port of [beUI OTP Input](https://beui.dev/components/blocks/otp-input). A one-time-code field whose digits roll into their slots, with an error shake and a check that draws itself on success.

```tsx
import { OTPInput } from "./src";

<OTPInput
  label="Verification code"
  hint="We sent a code to your phone."
  errorMessage="Wrong code, try again."
  successMessage="Verified."
  value={code}
  status={status}
  onChangeText={setCode}
  onComplete={verify}
/>
```

- **Slots:** `length` slots (6 by default), 48 by 56 points each. Each new digit rolls up into its slot over 220 ms, and a deleted digit rolls out upward. `mask` shows dots instead of digits.
- **Caret:** the active slot shows a blinking caret and a stronger border. Slot borders fade between empty, filled, active, error and success colours.
- **Status:** `status="error"` shakes the slots and turns them red. `status="success"` turns them green and springs in a check that draws itself beside the slots. Each status message is announced to screen readers.
- **Input:** a transparent native `TextInput` covers the slots and owns focus, the number pad, paste and SMS autofill (`oneTimeCode` on iOS, `sms-otp` on Android). It only accepts digits. `onComplete` fires when the last slot fills.
- **State:** pass `value` with `onChangeText` to control it, or `defaultValue` to let it manage itself.
- **Keyboard:** the number pad follows the app's light or dark theme on iOS (override with `keyboardAppearance`). `blurOnComplete` dismisses the keyboard once the last slot fills.
- **Accessibility:** screen readers see one field named by `label` (or "One-time passcode"), with the current message as its hint. The drawn slots are hidden from them.
- **Reduced motion:** when the system asks for it, or `disableAnimation` is set, digits and colours change instantly, the caret stays solid, and nothing shakes.

Unlike the web version, editing always happens at the end of the code: backspace removes the last digit and typing appends. The web version lets you place the caret in a middle slot with a mouse or the arrow keys, which touch keyboards don't offer.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-presence.ts`, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `hooks/use-shake.ts`, `primitives/drawn-path.tsx`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`.

components.title: Select
components.description: A panel that unfolds out of its trigger.
components.readme:
# Select

Native port of [beUI Select](https://beui.dev/components/motion/select). A panel that unfolds out of its trigger: it starts as a thin lip on the trigger's edge, grows to full height, then pulls 8 points away into its own card while the trigger's near corners square off and round back.

```tsx
import {
  Select,
  SelectContent,
  SelectItem,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
} from "./src";

<Select defaultValue="expo" onValueChange={setFramework}>
  <SelectTrigger accessibilityLabel="Framework">
    <SelectValue placeholder="Choose a framework" />
  </SelectTrigger>
  <SelectContent>
    <SelectItem value="expo">Expo</SelectItem>
    <SelectItem value="next">Next.js</SelectItem>
    <SelectItem value="legacy" disabled>Legacy</SelectItem>
  </SelectContent>
</Select>
```

## Parts

- **Select:** owns the state. `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange` for the selection, `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` for the panel, `disabled` for the whole control.
- **SelectTrigger:** the field. It's a combobox for screen readers and reports whether it's expanded. Its chevron turns as the panel opens.
- **SelectValue:** the chosen item's label, or `placeholder` in the muted color.
- **SelectContent:** the panel. It renders in a transparent modal at the trigger's position, so it draws over everything and isn't clipped by scroll views. A tap outside it, or Android's back button, closes it.
- **SelectItem:** an option. The selected one gets a drawn check. When its children aren't a plain string, give it a `label` for SelectValue and screen readers.

## Placement and long lists

The panel opens below the trigger, or above it when there isn't room below and there's more above. It's capped at 320 points and scrolls past that.

## Motion

Opening uses a short, barely bouncy spring (300 ms, damping ratio 0.88). Closing folds back over 200 ms with beUI's ease-out. Items fade in as the panel opens. With reduced motion, or `disableAnimation`, the panel appears and disappears without unfolding.

Copy this directory, `primitives/drawn-path.tsx`, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`.

components.title: Multi Select
components.description: Searchable options that become removable chips.
components.readme:
# Multi Select

Native port of [beUI Multi Select](https://beui.dev/components/motion/multi-select). Composable parts for picking several options from a searchable list. Picked options become removable chips that rise in, shrink away, and spring into new places.

```tsx
import {
  MultiSelect,
  MultiSelectContent,
  MultiSelectEmpty,
  MultiSelectGroup,
  MultiSelectInput,
  MultiSelectItem,
  MultiSelectLabel,
  MultiSelectList,
  MultiSelectTrigger,
  MultiSelectValue,
} from "./src";

<MultiSelect value={teams} onValueChange={setTeams}>
  <MultiSelectTrigger accessibilityLabel="Teams">
    <MultiSelectValue placeholder="Choose teams" />
  </MultiSelectTrigger>
  <MultiSelectContent>
    <MultiSelectInput accessibilityLabel="Search teams" />
    <MultiSelectList accessibilityLabel="Teams">
      <MultiSelectGroup>
        <MultiSelectLabel>Product teams</MultiSelectLabel>
        <MultiSelectItem value="design">Design</MultiSelectItem>
        <MultiSelectItem value="engineering" keywords={["dev"]}>
          Engineering
        </MultiSelectItem>
      </MultiSelectGroup>
      <MultiSelectEmpty>No teams found.</MultiSelectEmpty>
    </MultiSelectList>
  </MultiSelectContent>
</MultiSelect>
```

## Parts

- **MultiSelect:** owns the state. `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange` for the picked options, `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` for the list, `query` / `defaultQuery` / `onQueryChange` for the search text, and `filter` to replace the default in-order character match. `disabled`, `disableAnimation`.
- **MultiSelectTrigger:** the field. Chips wrap inside it beside a chevron, and a tap anywhere but a chip's X opens or closes the list. Give it an `accessibilityLabel`.
- **MultiSelectValue:** a chip for each picked option, with a remove button. `placeholder` shows while nothing is picked. Pass a function child to render chip labels yourself.
- **MultiSelectContent:** the floating panel. A tap outside it, or Android's back button, closes it.
- **MultiSelectInput:** a search field for the top of the panel. It filters the list as you type, return picks the top match, and Backspace in an empty search removes the last chip.
- **MultiSelectList:** scrolls past 256 points, or sooner when the room beside the field is tight.
- **MultiSelectGroup** and **MultiSelectLabel:** a group hides itself while a query leaves none of its options.
- **MultiSelectItem:** an option, shown as a checkbox row at least 44 points tall. `textValue` labels it when its children aren't a string; `keywords` adds words a query can match; `disabled` dims it.
- **MultiSelectEmpty** and **MultiSelectSeparator.**

## On native

Like the web version, the panel floats over the page beside the field without moving anything. It opens below the field, or above it when the room below is tight and there's more above; the keyboard counts against that room, and the list shortens to fit whatever is left.

The search field lives at the top of the panel rather than in the field: the panel is a modal, and a modal takes focus from inputs behind it. Chip labels stay correct while the panel is closed because MultiSelectContent keeps a hidden copy of the options mounted.

## Motion

The panel grows out of the field and pulls 6 points away on a spring with a light bounce (500 ms, damping ratio 0.78), then folds back over 200 ms. Chips rise 6 points and scale up from 92% as they're picked, shrink out over 160 ms as they're removed, and the rest spring into place on beUI's layout spring. Checks fade and scale in over 140 ms.

With reduced motion, or `disableAnimation`, the panel and chips change at once.

## Accessibility

The field reads as a button with its label, the picked options as its value, and the list's expanded state; the search field reads with its own label; each option as a checkbox with its checked and disabled state, and each chip's remove button as "Remove" and the option's label. Give the input an `accessibilityLabel`.

Copy this directory, `primitives/drawn-path.tsx`, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`.

components.title: Color Picker
components.description: A popover picker with a loupe under your finger.
components.readme:
# Color Picker

Native port of [beUI Color Picker](https://beui.dev/components/motion/color-picker), built for touch. A trigger opens a popover with a saturation and brightness area, where a loupe lifts above your finger while you drag, plus hue and opacity sliders, hex, RGB and HSL fields, and presets.

```tsx
import {
  ColorPicker,
  ColorPickerAlpha,
  ColorPickerArea,
  ColorPickerContent,
  ColorPickerHexInput,
  ColorPickerHue,
  ColorPickerPreset,
  ColorPickerPresets,
  ColorPickerSwatch,
  ColorPickerTrigger,
} from "./src";

<ColorPicker value={color} onValueChange={setColor} onValueCommit={save}>
  <ColorPickerTrigger />
  <ColorPickerContent accessibilityLabel="Brand color">
    <ColorPickerArea />
    <ColorPickerHue />
    <ColorPickerAlpha />
    <View className="flex-row gap-1.5">
      <ColorPickerHexInput />
      <ColorPickerSwatch />
    </View>
    <ColorPickerPresets accessibilityLabel="Presets">
      <ColorPickerPreset value="#3478f6" label="Blue" />
      <ColorPickerPreset value="#e55656" label="Red" />
    </ColorPickerPresets>
  </ColorPickerContent>
</ColorPicker>
```

## Parts

- **ColorPicker:** owns the color. `value` / `defaultValue` (hex, defaults to `#3478f6`) / `onValueChange` (every change, such as each step of a drag) / `onValueCommit` (when a change settles: a drag ends, a field is submitted, a preset is picked). `alpha` allows translucent colors and defaults to true. `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange`, `disabled`, `disableAnimation`.
- **ColorPickerTrigger:** a color chip and the hex.
- **ColorPickerContent:** the floating panel, below the trigger unless there's more room above. A tap outside, or Android's back button, closes it.
- **ColorPickerArea:** saturation and brightness. A finger down jumps the thumb there; dragging moves it.
- **ColorPickerHue** and **ColorPickerAlpha:** sliders with a tall touch area around the thin track. The opacity slider renders nothing when `alpha` is off.
- **ColorPickerHexInput:** updates live once six or eight digits are in, and shakes and reverts if what's left on submit isn't a color.
- **ColorPickerChannels:** numeric `rgb` or `hsl` fields, plus opacity when alpha is on.
- **ColorPickerSwatch:** the current color over a transparency checkerboard.
- **ColorPickerPresets** and **ColorPickerPreset:** swatches; a ring marks the one matching the current color.
- **useColorPicker():** the color as HSVA, RGBA and hex, with `update`, `commit`, `open` and `setOpen`, for custom parts. The color helpers `parseHex`, `formatHex`, `hsvaToRgba` and `rgbaToHsva` are exported too.

The parts also work inline, without a trigger: put the area and sliders straight inside `ColorPicker`.

## Motion

The panel opens like a native popover: it springs out of the trigger's corner (scaling up from 90%, fading in and dropping 8 points) on a quick, lightly damped spring, and its rows settle in just behind it. Opening waits until the panel is actually on screen, since a modal takes a moment to appear. Closing runs the same path back as a 160 ms fade with a fixed end, so the modal is gone the moment it finishes and the next tap lands on the page.

While a finger is on the area or a slider, the thumb follows it directly on the UI thread and tucks in, and a teardrop loupe lifts above it with a little overshoot, showing the color under the finger and swinging with the drag's speed. It drops when the finger lifts. When the color changes from elsewhere, the thumbs glide there on beUI's glide spring. The preset ring hops between swatches over a low arc, higher for longer jumps.

While a field is focused, the panel lifts clear of the keyboard.

The web version morphs the trigger's chip into the area, blurs rows as they arrive and has an eye dropper. On a phone, the morph reads as a block of color sweeping over the panel, React Native has no cheap blur, and there's no system color sampler, so the panel opens as a popover, rows fade and drop instead, and there's no eye dropper. With reduced motion, or `disableAnimation`, the panel fades in place, thumbs jump, and there's no loupe.

## Accessibility

The area is an adjustable control: swipe up and down to change saturation, with Brighter and Darker as extra actions, and it reads both values. The sliders are adjustable too, with their own names and values. Presets read their color's name and whether they're selected. Fields have labels. Give the trigger an `accessibilityLabel` that names the color's purpose.

For haptics, call your haptics library from `onValueCommit`, as the showcase does with expo-haptics.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `hooks/use-shake.ts`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`.

components.description: A checkmark that draws itself in.

files.content:
export type { CheckboxProps } from "./checkbox";
export { Checkbox } from "./checkbox";

components.readme:
# Checkbox

Native port of [beUI Checkbox](https://beui.dev/components/motion/checkbox). A form choice with a checkmark that draws itself in, spring press feedback, and an indeterminate state.

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from "./src";

<Checkbox checked={accepted} onCheckedChange={setAccepted} label="Accept terms and conditions" />
<Checkbox label="Email me updates" description="One message a month." />
<Checkbox checked={all} indeterminate={some} onCheckedChange={toggleAll} label="Select all" />
```

- **Mark:** the checkmark draws itself in over 300 ms, and the indeterminate dash over 200 ms. The mark fades and scales in from 50%. When `indeterminate` turns on or off, the check and the dash crossfade.
- **Colours:** the fill and border fade between the idle and primary colours over 200 ms.
- **Press:** the box springs to 92% on beUI's `SPRING_PRESS` spring.
- **State:** pass `checked` with `onCheckedChange` to control it, or `defaultChecked` to let it manage itself. As on the web, pressing calls `onCheckedChange(!checked)`; an indeterminate checkbox decides what "select all" means through that handler.
- **Label and description:** `label` is the spoken name, and `description` is read as the accessibility hint. The box and text form one touch target, and `hitSlop` tops a 20-point row up to 48 points.
- **Accessibility:** reports the `checkbox` role. An indeterminate checkbox reports a mixed state.
- **Reduced motion:** when the system asks for it, or `disableAnimation` is set, the mark and colours change instantly with no press scale.

The mark is drawn by the shared `DrawnPath` primitive with rotated Views, matching the web SVG path, so the component needs no SVG library.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-presence.ts`, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `primitives/drawn-path.tsx`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`.

components.description: One dot glides to the option you pick.

components.readme:
# Radio Group

Native port of [beUI Radio Group](https://beui.dev/components/motion/radio). A single-select group whose indicator dot glides to the option you pick.

```tsx
import { RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "./src";

<RadioGroup value={plan} onValueChange={setPlan}>
  <RadioGroupItem value="starter" label="Starter, free" />
  <RadioGroupItem value="pro" label="Pro, $12/mo" description="Unlimited projects." />
  <RadioGroupItem value="legacy" label="Legacy plan" disabled />
</RadioGroup>

<RadioGroup defaultValue="md" orientation="horizontal">…</RadioGroup>
```

- **Glide:** one dot belongs to the group. It springs to the selected ring on beUI's `SPRING_LAYOUT` spring, which replaces the web version's shared `layoutId`. The first selection appears in place without travelling.
- **Press:** the ring springs to 92%. When you press the selected option, the dot presses with it.
- **State:** pass `value` with `onValueChange` to control it, or `defaultValue` to let it manage itself. `orientation` stacks items vertically (the default) or wraps them in a row.
- **Label and description:** `label` is the spoken name, and `description` is read as the accessibility hint. Each item's ring and text form one touch target, and `hitSlop` tops a 20-point row up to 48 points.
- **Accessibility:** the group reports the `radiogroup` role and each item reports `radio` with its checked and disabled states.
- **Reduced motion:** when the system asks for it, or `disableAnimation` is set on the group, the dot and colours change instantly with no press scale.

Items measure their position relative to the group, so they can sit inside your own wrapper views. Each item re-measures when its own layout or the group's layout changes. If an item moves without either of those changing, the dot can be left behind until the next layout.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`.

components.readme:
# Range Slider

Native port of [beUI Range Slider](https://beui.dev/components/motion/range-slider). A stepped slider with tick dots and a bar thumb that glides between steps and stretches while held.

```tsx
import { RangeSlider } from "./src";

const [value, setValue] = useState(40);

<RangeSlider
  value={value}
  onValueChange={setValue}
  step={5}
  accessibilityLabel="Value"
/>
```

## Props

- `value` / `defaultValue` / `onValueChange`: controlled or uncontrolled. `onValueChange` fires once per step while dragging, so it's the place for a selection haptic.
- `onSlidingComplete`: the final value when a drag or tap lets go.
- `min`, `max`, `step`: default to 0, 100 and 1. When the step doesn't divide the range, the end of the track still reaches `max`.
- `showTicks`: a dot at each step. Defaults to true, and hides itself past 50 steps.
- `formatValueText`: what screen readers hear instead of the raw number, such as ``(v) => `${v}%` ``.
- `disabled`, `disableAnimation`, `className`.

## Touch

Drag or tap anywhere on the track; the thumb lands under your finger. Horizontal drags own the slider and vertical swipes go on to scroll the page, so it works inside a ScrollView.

## Motion

The thumb and fill follow beUI's glide spring, critically damped so they never rebound off an end. While held, the thumb stretches to 135% on a bouncy spring. With reduced motion, or `disableAnimation`, both move straight to the value and the thumb doesn't stretch.

## Accessibility

The track is one adjustable control (a `slider` on web) with its range, value and value text. VoiceOver and TalkBack swipe up and down to step it; on web, arrow keys step it, Page Up and Down move ten steps, and Home and End jump to the ends. Give it an `accessibilityLabel`.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`.

components.readme:
# Switch

Native port of [beUI Switch](https://beui.dev/components/motion/switch). A toggle with a heavy spring-driven thumb and press feedback.

```tsx
import { Switch } from "./src";

<Switch checked={enabled} onCheckedChange={setEnabled} label="Enable notifications" />
<Switch defaultChecked label="Uncontrolled" />
<Switch accessibilityLabel="Airplane mode" />
```

- **Motion:** the thumb travels on the web version's heavy spring (stiffness 800, damping 80, mass 4), so it feels weighty without wobbling. The track colour fades between `bg-muted/60` and `bg-primary` over 200 ms.
- **Press:** while pressed, the thumb shrinks to 90% and stretches 4 points toward where it is going.
- **Disabled:** dims to 60% opacity and ignores presses. On iOS and Android, pressing a disabled switch gives the thumb a small shake. On web the shake is skipped, because react-native-web needs the real `disabled` prop to report the disabled state.
- **State:** pass `checked` with `onCheckedChange` to control it, or `defaultChecked` to let it manage itself.
- **Label:** `label` renders text beside the track. The track and label form one touch target, and the label becomes the spoken name. Without a label, pass `accessibilityLabel`.
- **Accessibility:** reports the `switch` role with its checked and disabled states. `hitSlop` tops the 28-point track up to a 48-point touch area.
- **RTL:** the thumb starts and travels from the leading edge.
- **Reduced motion:** when the system asks for it, or `disableAnimation` is set, the thumb and colour change instantly with no press squish or shake.

The web Switch only responds to taps, and so does this one. Native platform switches can also be dragged; that may come later with Gesture Handler.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`.

components.title: Bouncy Accordion
components.description: FAQ rows that spring apart as they open.
components.readme:
# Bouncy Accordion

Native port of [beUI Bouncy Accordion](https://beui.dev/components/motion/bouncy-accordion). A single-open accordion for FAQs and settings: rows sit together in one rounded stack, and the open row springs apart into its own group while its content bounces open.

```tsx
import { BouncyAccordion } from "./src";

<BouncyAccordion
  items={[
    { id: "expo", title: "Does it work in Expo Go?", description: "Yes." },
    { id: "icons", title: "Which icons?", description: "Any library.", icon: Search },
  ]}
  defaultValue="expo"
/>
```

- **Grouping:** closed rows join into one stack with 28-point outer corners. Opening a row moves it 12 points away from its neighbors, and the corners on either side of each gap spring round, so the open row becomes its own card.
- **Motion:** the gap, corners and content height spring with a bounce: 550 ms at damping ratio 0.62 for the row, 580 ms at 0.68 to open, and 520 ms at 0.55 to close. That's livelier than the web version on close, where the bounce is mostly clipped once the height reaches zero. The chevron flips on its own spring and the content fades in over 180 ms. A row that starts open appears in place without animating.
- **Closing bounce:** a height can't go below zero, so a closing row's overshoot becomes a small negative bottom margin. The rows below travel up to 14 points past rest and spring back. That overlap only covers the closing row's empty bottom padding, in the same colour as the stack it's rejoining, so nothing visibly overlaps.
- **Content:** `description` can be a string, which gets the default muted text style, or any element. Its height is measured at its natural size, so long answers and larger text open fully.
- **State:** pass `value` with `onValueChange` to control the open row, or `defaultValue` to let it manage itself. `collapsible={false}` keeps one row always open.
- **Rows:** each row is at least 54 points tall, with an optional leading `icon` (a component given `{ size, color }`, or an element) and a soft pressed highlight. `disabled` dims a row and ignores presses.
- **Accessibility:** each row header is a button reporting its expanded and disabled states. Closed content is hidden from screen readers.
- **Reduced motion:** when the system asks for it, or `disableAnimation` is set, rows open and close instantly.

`classNames` styles the root, rows, headers, titles and descriptions individually.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `primitives/drawn-path.tsx`, `primitives/render-icon.tsx`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`.

components.title: Tabs
components.description: Pill, segment and underline with a gliding indicator.
components.readme:
# Tabs

Native port of [beUI Tabs](https://beui.dev/components/motion/tabs). Pill, segment or underline tabs with an indicator that springs between them.

```tsx
import { Tabs, TabsContent, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from "./src";

<Tabs defaultValue="overview">
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTrigger value="overview">Overview</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="activity">Activity</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsContent value="overview">…</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value="activity">…</TabsContent>
</Tabs>

<Tabs value={range} onValueChange={setRange} variant="segment">…</Tabs>
```

- **Variants:** `pill` (the default), `segment` and `underline`.
- **Indicator:** one indicator per list springs to the selected tab. It uses the web version's spring (stiffness 245, damping 36, mass 1.2), which settles without overshooting the list edges. The first selection appears in place.
- **Label colour:** in the pill and segment variants, each label has a second copy in the on-primary colour, clipped to wherever the indicator overlaps it. During a glide, the colour changes exactly at the indicator's edge, matching the web version's clip-path technique.
- **Overflow:** a list wider than its container scrolls sideways. Each edge with tabs past it fades into the list's background, and selecting a tab scrolls it 32 points clear of the edge so it sits beyond the fade. On native, swiping replaces the web version's arrow buttons. The fades use `experimental_backgroundImage` gradients on iOS and Android, and `backgroundImage` on web.
- **Content:** `TabsContent` renders only the active panel, fading it in and rising 4 points over 180 ms.
- **State:** pass `value` with `onValueChange` to control it, or `defaultValue` to let it manage itself. `TabsTrigger` accepts `disabled`.
- **Accessibility:** the list reports the `tablist` role, and each trigger reports `tab` with its selected and disabled states. The overlay label copy is hidden from screen readers.
- **Reduced motion:** when the system asks for it, or `disableAnimation` is set on `Tabs`, the indicator jumps to its new tab and content fades without rising.

Triggers must be direct children of `TabsList`, because each trigger measures its own position in the list. Text children are coloured for each state. Other elements, such as icons, render as given.

`indicatorClassName` on `TabsList` overrides the indicator colour.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`.

components.title: Swipeable List
components.description: Rows that swipe to reveal actions.
components.readme:
# Swipeable List

List rows that swipe left or right to reveal actions, built for touch first: actions stretch with your finger, and a full swipe runs the outermost action as the row slides away. It started as a port of [beUI Swipeable List](https://beui.dev/components/blocks/swipeable-list) and now goes further than the web version.

```tsx
import { SwipeableList } from "./src";

<SwipeableList
  items={[
    {
      id: "brief",
      title: "Launch brief",
      description: "Finalize the announcement copy",
      meta: "9:41",
      leftActions: [
        { id: "done", label: "Done", icon: Check, tone: "success" },
        { id: "pin", label: "Pin", icon: Pin, tone: "primary" },
      ],
      rightActions: [
        { id: "later", label: "Later", icon: Clock, tone: "warning" },
        { id: "trash", label: "Trash", icon: Trash, tone: "danger" },
      ],
    },
  ]}
  onAction={({ item, action }) => {
    if (action.id === "trash") remove(item.id);
  }}
  onSwipeThreshold={({ armed }) => armed && Haptics.impactAsync()}
  onItemPress={(item) => open(item)}
/>
```

## Gestures

- **Swipe:** each row follows a Gesture Handler pan. A horizontal drag claims the row, and a vertical drag leaves the surrounding scroll view scrolling.
- **Stretching actions:** as you drag, the revealed space is shared evenly between that side's actions. Each action is a filled panel tinted by `tone` (`neutral`, `primary`, `success`, `warning` or `danger`), and its icon and label fade and scale in once there is room for them.
- **Resting open:** releasing past 40% of a side's actions (or flicking faster than 600 points per second) rests the row open at `actionWidth` per action (72 by default). An open row closes below 60%, on a flick back, or on a tap.
- **Full swipe:** keep dragging past the resting actions (by 64 points, and at least 55% of the row) and the outermost action springs out to fill the whole revealed space, while the others fold away. Releasing slides the row off screen and runs that action. Drag back before releasing and it springs back to normal. The outermost action is the first in `leftActions` and the last in `rightActions`. Set `fullSwipe={false}` to turn this off.
- **Resistance:** past the furthest point a side allows, the row moves less the further you pull, like iOS rubber-banding.
- **One open row:** starting a swipe on another row closes the open one.

## Removal

When an action removes its item from `items`, the row collapses its height and spacing while it fades, and the rows below glide up on a spring. After a full swipe the row is already off screen, so it simply folds away. If a fully swiped action does not remove its item, the row returns to rest. Items added later fade in; items present on first render appear in place.

## Callbacks

- `onAction({ item, action, side, fullSwipe })` runs for tapped actions, full swipes and accessibility actions. `fullSwipe` tells them apart.
- `onSwipeThreshold({ item, side, armed })` fires as a drag crosses the full-swipe point in either direction, the moment to play a haptic. The component itself has no haptics dependency. The example app calls `expo-haptics` here.
- `onItemPress(item)` runs when a closed row is tapped, with a soft pressed highlight.

## Other details

- **State:** pass `value` with `onValueChange` to control which row is open, or `defaultValue` to let it manage itself.
- **Content:** rows show `leading`, `title`, `description` and `meta` by default. Use `content` on an item, or `renderItem` for the whole list, to supply your own.
- **Accessibility:** each row is one element named by its title, description and meta. Screen readers can't swipe, so every action is also an accessibility action on the row (VoiceOver's rotor, or TalkBack's actions menu), along with "activate" when `onItemPress` is set. Action buttons stay hidden until their side opens.
- **Reduced motion:** when the system asks for it, or `disableAnimation` is set, rows snap without springing and removals happen without the collapse.
- **Web:** gestures and full swipes work. React Native Web doesn't run custom exit animations, so removed rows disappear without collapsing.

The list renders every row in a plain View, which suits inboxes and queues of tens of rows. Very long lists would need a virtualized variant built on `FlatList`.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `primitives/render-icon.tsx`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`. The host app needs Gesture Handler with a `GestureHandlerRootView` at its root, which the example app already has.

components.title: Number Animation
components.description: Rolling tickers and count-ups.
components.readme:
# Number Animation

Native port of [beUI Number Animation](https://beui.dev/components/motion/number): two primitives for numbers that change.

```tsx
import { AnimatedNumber, NumberTicker } from "./src";

<NumberTicker value={users} locale className="text-3xl font-semibold text-foreground" />
<AnimatedNumber value={revenue} format={(n) => `$${Math.round(n).toLocaleString()}`} />
```

## NumberTicker

Each digit sits in a 0–9 column and rolls to its new value over 900 ms on beUI's ease-out curve. On the first appearance, digits roll up from 0 one after another, 40 ms apart. Later updates roll every changed digit at once, because a stagger on live data reads as lag. Columns belong to a place value (ones, tens, hundreds), so a growing number adds columns on the left without replaying the others. Supports `pad`, `prefix`, `suffix`, `locale` grouping and a custom `format`.

## AnimatedNumber

Counts from the previous value (0 at first) to `value` over 1200 ms on the ease-out curve, formatting every frame with `format`. An interrupted count continues from where it is. Screen readers get the final value, never the in-between frames.

## Shared behavior

- `className` styles every glyph, such as `text-3xl font-semibold text-foreground`. Digits are tabular, and their roll height is measured from a "0" in that style, so it follows font size and text scaling.
- Each component is one accessible text element whose label is the full final value.
- Reduced motion, or `disableAnimation`, shows the final value without rolling or counting.
- Durations are in milliseconds. The web version's `startOnView` and `blur` options aren't ported: these start when mounted, and native has no cheap blur.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts` and `styles/motion.ts`.

components.title: Text Animation
components.description: Reveals, sweeps, shimmers, cascades and scrambles.
components.readme:
# Text Animation

Native port of [beUI Text Animation](https://beui.dev/components/motion/text-animation): five primitives for text that arrives or changes.

```tsx
import {
  ChromaticTextReveal,
  TextCascade,
  TextReveal,
  TextScramble,
  TextShimmer,
} from "./src";

<TextReveal text="Motion in words." className="text-3xl font-semibold text-foreground" />
<ChromaticTextReveal prefix="Motion that feels" words={["natural.", "alive."]} />
<TextShimmer className="text-xl font-semibold">Thinking</TextShimmer>
<TextCascade text={status} />
<TextScramble text={codename} />
```

## TextReveal

Words (or characters with `split="char"`) rise into place one after another, 90 ms apart. Each rises on a soft spring (stiffness 140, damping 26, mass 1.2) and fades in over 700 ms. `yOffset` takes points or a percentage of the line height ("40%" by default). Lines wrap between words, never inside them. Pass an array for explicit lines. Change `key` to replay it.

## ChromaticTextReveal

A fixed `prefix` followed by a word revealed by a moving colour sweep. Behind the sweep the word is solid, inside a trail 14% of the word either side it takes the `colors` palette, and ahead of it the word is still invisible. After each 1200 ms sweep and an 800 ms pause, the next word arrives. The space reserved is the widest word's, so the sentence never reflows.

## TextShimmer

A highlight that sweeps across muted text every 2500 ms, for loading and thinking states. The colours come from the theme's muted and foreground tokens.

## TextCascade

The letter cascade from `StatefulButton` for standalone text. When `text` changes, the old letters roll up and away as the new ones spring in from below, left to right, and the width springs to fit.

## TextScramble

When `text` changes, every unresolved character cycles through random glyphs, settling left to right on the new text within 420–760 ms. The first text appears as is.

## Shared behavior

- `className` styles every glyph or word, such as `text-xl font-semibold text-foreground`.
- Each component is one accessible text element whose label is the final text.
- Reduced motion, or `disableAnimation`, shows text without movement. TextReveal fades, ChromaticTextReveal stays on the first word fully revealed, TextShimmer stays muted, TextCascade crossfades, and TextScramble swaps instantly.
- Durations are in milliseconds.

Native can't clip a gradient to text without extra libraries. The chromatic sweep and the shimmer therefore colour each character individually from the moving gradient, using the shared `GlyphRow` primitive. Scripts that need letter shaping, such as Arabic or Devanagari, are coloured as a whole instead, so their letters still join. TextCascade cascades only Latin text for the same reason. Native also has no cheap blur, so the web version's blur effects are left out. `whileInView` and `startOnView` aren't ported: animations start when mounted.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-presence.ts`, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `primitives/cascade-text.tsx`, `primitives/glyph-row.tsx`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`.

components.title: Alert
components.description: Feedback that eases in and folds away.
components.readme:
# Alert

Native port of [beUI Animated Alert](https://beui.dev/components/motion/alert). Composable feedback that eases in, blends between variants, and folds away when dismissed.

```tsx
import {
  Alert,
  AlertAction,
  AlertClose,
  AlertContent,
  AlertDescription,
  AlertIcon,
  AlertTitle,
} from "./src";

<Alert variant="destructive" open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
  <AlertIcon />
  <AlertContent>
    <AlertTitle>Something went wrong</AlertTitle>
    <AlertDescription>We couldn't save your changes.</AlertDescription>
    <AlertAction>
      <Button size="sm" variant="outline" onPress={retry}>Try again</Button>
    </AlertAction>
  </AlertContent>
  <AlertClose />
</Alert>
```

## Parts

- **Alert:** the surface. `variant` is `default`, `info`, `success`, `warning` or `destructive`, each from the semantic tokens. `open` / `defaultOpen` / `onOpenChange` control visibility; it starts open. `contentClassName` styles the inner row.
- **AlertIcon:** the variant's icon. Pass children to replace it.
- **AlertContent:** stacks the title, description and actions, and takes the free width.
- **AlertTitle:** takes the variant's color. **AlertDescription:** muted supporting text.
- **AlertAction:** a row for buttons.
- **AlertClose:** a 32-point X button (44 with its hit slop) that dismisses the alert after running your `onPress`.
- **useAlert():** `open`, `variant`, `setOpen` and `dismiss`, for custom parts.

## Motion

Opening fades in over 180 ms and drops 6 points into place over 200 ms, both on beUI's ease-out, while the space it needs springs open. Closing fades and lifts over 120 ms as the space folds away over 220 ms, so whatever sits below glides up instead of jumping. That fold is a native addition; the web version leaves the space to its container.

Changing variant blends the surface color over 200 ms, swaps the icon with a 4-point rise and slight scale, and springs the height to fit new content.

With reduced motion, or `disableAnimation`, the alert fades without moving and its space opens and closes at once.

## Accessibility

Warning and destructive alerts are announced as alerts and interrupt; the others are polite live regions. A closed alert is hidden from screen readers while it folds away. Override either with `accessibilityRole` or `accessibilityLiveRegion`.

Copy this directory, `primitives/drawn-path.tsx`, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`.

components.title: Animated Badge
components.description: Status pills whose icon and label roll.
components.readme:
# Animated Badge

Native port of [beUI Animated Badge](https://beui.dev/components/motion/animated-badge). A status pill whose icon and label roll when they change, with colors that blend and a width that springs to fit.

```tsx
import { AnimatedBadge } from "./src";

<AnimatedBadge status={synced ? "success" : "loading"} accessibilityLiveRegion="polite">
  {synced ? "Synced" : "Syncing"}
</AnimatedBadge>
```

## Props

- `status`: `neutral` (the default), `info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` or `loading`. Each uses the semantic tokens, so badges follow the theme.
- `size`: `sm` (24 points tall) or `md` (32, the default).
- `children`: the label. Leave it out for an icon-only badge, and give that an `accessibilityLabel`.
- `icon`: replaces the status icon. A component given `{ size, color }`, or an element.
- `showIcon`: defaults to true.
- `pulse`: a slow breathing fill. On by default while loading.
- `contentKey`: rolls the label when it changes. Defaults to a string or number label, so a new label rolls on its own; pass one when the label is an element.
- `disableAnimation`, `className`, plus any View props.

The badge hugs its content. Give it a `self-*` class, such as `self-center`, to place it in a column.

## Motion

On a status or label change, the leaving icon and label slide up and fade over 140 ms on beUI's ease-out, while the next ones rise into place on the swap spring. Colors blend over 300 ms and the pill springs to its new width on the layout spring. The loading icon spins once a second and the pulse breathes every 1.6 seconds.

The web version also blurs content as it rolls; React Native has no cheap blur, so the roll fades instead.

With reduced motion, or `disableAnimation`, content swaps in place, colors change at once, and the spin and pulse stop.

## Accessibility

The badge reads as one piece of text: its label, or `accessibilityLabel`. Icons are hidden from screen readers. For a badge that changes while someone is on the screen, pass `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"` on Android; on iOS, announce the change with `AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility` if it matters.

Copy this directory, `primitives/drawn-path.tsx`, `primitives/render-icon.tsx`, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`.

components.description: Seventeen indicators from one size prop.

files.content:
export type { LoaderProps, LoaderVariant } from "./loader";
export { Loader } from "./loader";

components.readme:
# Loader

Native port of [beUI Loader](https://beui.dev/components/motion/loader). Seventeen loading indicators that all scale from one `size`.

```tsx
import { Loader } from "./src";

<Loader />
<Loader variant="dots" size={24} />
<Loader variant="helix" speed={1.4} className="text-primary" />
<Loader variant="ascii-braille" label="Thinking" />
```

**Variants:** `spinner`, `dots`, `bars`, `dot-matrix`, `dither`, `morph`, `comet`, `scramble`, `metaballs`, `newton`, `helix`, `percent`, and the terminal-style `ascii`, `ascii-line`, `ascii-braille`, `ascii-blocks` and `ascii-bounce`.

- **Size and speed:** `size` (32 points by default) sets the square everything scales from. `speed` is seconds per cycle (1 by default), matching the web prop.
- **Color:** the theme's foreground colour by default. Pass a colour utility in `className` (such as `text-primary`) or a `color` value.
- **Motion:** every variant uses the web version's timings, keyframes and stagger on beUI's in-out curve.
- **Accessibility:** the loader is one element with the `progressbar` role and a busy state. `label` ("Loading" by default) is its spoken name.
- **Reduced motion:** when the system asks for it, or `disableAnimation` is set, movement is replaced by a calm opacity pulse. ASCII frames and the percent counter slow down instead of stopping, because they swap content rather than move it. Newton stays still.

The web version draws three variants with SVG. Here they're drawn with Views, so the component needs no SVG library:
- **Spinner:** the arc is the top border of a ring, so its ends are square rather than round.
- **Morph:** cycles through a circle, square, diamond and squircle using corner radius and rotation, rather than morphing SVG paths. It doesn't have the web version's triangle or hexagon.
- **Metaballs:** two dots cross while a blob swells where they meet, standing in for the SVG goo filter.

Copy this directory, `hooks/use-reduced-motion.ts`, `styles/motion.ts`, and the semantic tokens in `styles/theme.css`.
